The Trust shall obtain all necessary permissions for the use of third-party copyrighted material, including archival photographs and published works, and shall provide evidence of such permissions to the Grants Secretariat upon request.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Trust may use Project materials for its own archival and promotional purposes, provided that such use is consistent with the acknowledgement requirements set out in Clause 11.

**17. Insurance and Indemnity**

The Trust shall maintain, at its own cost, comprehensive public liability insurance for the duration of the Project, with coverage of not less than SGD 1,000,000.00 per occurrence. The Trust shall also maintain insurance for all staff and volunteers engaged in the Project, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Grants Secretariat upon request.

The Trust shall indemnify the Board and the Laksamana Grant Programme against all claims, losses, damages, and expenses arising from any act or omission of the Trust, its staff, volunteers, or contractors in connection with the Project, except where such claims arise from the negligence of the Board.

The Trust shall use its best endeavours to ensure that all Project activities, including but not limited to public programmes, exhibitions, research, and documentation, are concluded by the Project End Date.

The Trust shall notify the Grants Secretariat in writing, no later than fourteen (14) days prior to the Project End Date, of the anticipated date of completion of all Project activities. Such notification shall not constitute a request for an extension of time and shall be provided for planning purposes only.

**19. Extension of Time**

The Board may, at its sole discretion, consider a written request from the Trust for an extension of the Project End Date. Any such request must be submitted to the Grants Secretariat at least sixty (60) days before the Project End Date and must set out:

(a) the reasons for the delay, including any circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the Trust;

(b) a revised schedule for completion of the remaining Project activities; and

(c) confirmation that the extension will not result in an increase in the Grant Amount.

The Board shall not be obliged to grant any extension, and the Trust shall continue to comply with all other obligations under this Agreement pending the Board's decision. For the avoidance of doubt, no extension shall operate to extend the period for submission of the Final Report set out in Clause 21.

**20. Variation of Scope**

The Trust shall not make any material change to the scope, objectives, or deliverables of the Project without the prior written consent of the Board. A request for variation shall be submitted in writing, accompanied by a detailed explanation of the proposed change and its impact on the Project timeline, budget, and expected outcomes.

The Board may approve, reject, or approve with conditions any proposed variation. Any approved variation shall be recorded in a written addendum to this Agreement and shall not take effect until such addendum is signed by both parties.

**21. Final Report and Financial Reconciliation**

Within sixty (60) days after the Project End Date, the Trust shall submit to the Grants Secretariat the following:

(a) a final narrative report (the "Final Report") in the format prescribed by the Board, describing the activities undertaken, the outputs delivered, and the outcomes achieved against the objectives set out in the approved Proposal;

(b) a financial report (the "Financial Report") in the format prescribed by the Board, setting out all income and expenditure in respect of the Project, supported by a statement of accounts certified by the Trust's authorised signatory;

(c) a declaration, in the form prescribed by the Board, confirming that the Grant Amount has been applied solely for the purposes of the Project and in accordance with this Agreement; and

(d) copies of all relevant supporting documents, including invoices, receipts, and attendance records, as may be reasonably requested by the Grants Secretariat.

The Financial Report shall reconcile the Grant Amount disbursed to the Trust against verified expenditure. Any unspent portion of the Grant Amount shall be refunded to the Board within thirty (30) days of the Board's acceptance of the Financial Report. The Trust shall not use the Grant Amount to defray any expenditure incurred after the Project End Date unless the Board has given prior written approval.

**22. Final Report Approval and Release of Final Payment**

The final payment under Clause 15 shall be released only after the Board has approved the Final Report and the Financial Report. The Board shall notify the Trust in writing of its decision within sixty (60) days of receipt of the complete reports. If the Board does not approve the reports, it shall provide reasons and afford the Trust a reasonable opportunity to rectify any deficiencies and resubmit.
**23. Audit and Inspection**

The Board, through the Grants Secretariat or its authorised representatives, may at any reasonable time, and upon giving the Trust not less than seven (7) days' written notice, inspect the Project premises and the Trust's books, records, and accounts relating to the Project. The Trust shall provide all reasonable assistance and access to such personnel as may be necessary for the conduct of any audit, review, or inspection. Where the Board has reasonable grounds to suspect that the Grant Amount has not been applied in accordance with this Agreement, the Board may undertake an audit or inspection without prior notice.

The Trust shall retain all records, receipts, and supporting documents relating to the Project for a period of not less than five (5) years from the date of the Board's acceptance of the Financial Report. The Trust shall make available, upon request, the original documents and any electronic records for examination and copying.

**24. Intellectual Property**

Where the Project produces any materials, publications, images, or other outputs (collectively, the "Project Outputs"), the Trust shall ensure that the Project Outputs are made available to the public for non-commercial purposes, unless otherwise approved in writing by the Board. The Trust shall acknowledge the support of the Board and the Laksamana Grant Programme in all Project Outputs, in a form approved by the Grants Secretariat. Any copyright or other intellectual property rights in the Project Outputs shall remain with the Trust, subject to a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence in favour of the Board to use the Project Outputs for the purposes of publicity, reporting, and evaluation.

**25. Publicity and Acknowledgement**

The Trust shall not issue any press release, public statement, or promotional material referring to the Grant or the Project without first obtaining the written approval of the Grants Secretariat. The Trust shall ensure that all publicity materials comply with the branding guidelines issued by the Board from time to time. The Trust shall include, in any publication or material produced with the support of the Grant, the statement: "This project is supported by the Laksamana Grant Programme, a Heritage Fund initiative of the Board."

**26. Confidentiality**

The Trust shall keep confidential all information disclosed by the Board in connection with this Agreement and shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Board, except where such disclosure is required by law or by any regulatory authority. This obligation shall survive the termination or expiry of this Agreement.

**27. Data Protection**

The Trust shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (No. 26 of 2012) and any subsidiary legislation in relation to the collection, use, and disclosure of personal data in connection with the Project. The Trust shall put in place appropriate safeguards to protect personal data against unauthorised access, use, or disclosure.

**28. Anti-Bribery and Corruption**

The Trust shall not, and shall ensure that its officers, employees, and agents do not, offer, give, or receive any bribe, kickback, or other improper advantage in connection with the Project or this Agreement. The Trust shall notify the Board immediately if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected breach of this Clause 28.

**29. Conflict of Interest**

The Trust shall declare to the Board, in writing, any actual or potential conflict of interest that arises in connection with the Project, including any interest of the Trust's officers, employees, or board members in any supplier, contractor, or beneficiary of the Project. The Trust shall take all reasonable steps to manage and mitigate any such conflict in accordance with its internal policies and the requirements of the Board.

**30. Termination**

The Board may terminate this Agreement and suspend the payment of any undisbursed portion of the Grant Amount by giving written notice to the Trust if:
**30. Termination (continued)**

The Board may terminate this Agreement and suspend the payment of any undisbursed portion of the Grant Amount by giving written notice to the Trust if:

(a) the Trust fails to remedy a material breach of this Agreement within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice of such breach from the Board;

(b) the Trust becomes insolvent, enters into liquidation, or has a receiver or judicial manager appointed over any of its assets;

(c) the Trust ceases to carry on its operations or is unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement;

(d) the Trust provides false or misleading information to the Board in connection with the application for the Grant or the administration of the Grant Amount; or

(e) the Board determines, in its reasonable discretion, that the Project is no longer viable or that the continued disbursement of the Grant Amount would not serve the heritage conservation objectives of the Laksamana Grant Programme.

Upon termination, the Trust shall promptly return to the Board any undisbursed portion of the Grant Amount and shall account for all expenditures incurred up to the date of termination. The Board may require the Trust to repay any portion of the Grant Amount that has been disbursed but not expended in accordance with the Approved Budget and this Agreement.

**31. Force Majeure**

Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement where such failure or delay is caused by an event beyond the reasonable control of that party, including but not limited to fire, flood, storm, epidemic, pandemic, earthquake, civil unrest, war, or any act of government or public authority. The party affected shall notify the other party in writing as soon as practicable and shall take all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact of the event. If the event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either party may terminate this Agreement by giving fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other party.

**32. Notices**

All notices and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered by hand, registered post, or email to the addresses set out in this Agreement. Notices shall be deemed to have been received: if delivered by hand, at the time of delivery; if sent by registered post, on the fifth (5th) business day after posting; and if sent by email, at the time of transmission, provided that no delivery failure notification is received.

**33. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution**

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Singapore. The parties shall use their best efforts to resolve any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement through good-faith negotiations. If the dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of written notice by either party, the dispute shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration in Singapore in accordance with the Arbitration Rules of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ("SIAC") for the time being in force, which rules are deemed to be incorporated by reference into this Clause. The seat of arbitration shall be Singapore. The language of the arbitration shall be English. The Tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator, unless the parties agree otherwise. The decision of the Tribunal shall be final and binding on both parties.

**34. Entire Agreement**

This Agreement, together with the Schedules and any other documents expressly referred to herein, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the Project and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral.

**35. Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

The Trust shall maintain, at its own cost, comprehensive public liability insurance for the duration of the Project, with coverage of not less than SGD 1,000,000.00 per occurrence. The Trust shall also maintain insurance for all staff and volunteers engaged in the Project, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Grants Secretariat upon request.

**18. Project End Date and Completion**

The Project shall be completed by the Project End Date of **30 June 2026** (the "Project End Date"). The grant contract specifies that the Tales of the Tidal Canal project end date is 2026-06-30. Record status: current. The Trust shall use its best endeavours to ensure that all Project activities, including but not limited to public programmes, exhibitions, research, and documentation, are concluded by the Project End Date.

The Trust shall notify the Grants Secretariat in writing, no later than fourteen (14) days prior to the Project End Date, of the anticipated date of completion of all Project activities. Such notification shall not constitute a request for an extension of time and shall be provided for planning purposes only.

**19. Extension of Time**

The Board may, at its sole discretion, consider a written request from the Trust for an extension of the Project End Date. Any such request must be submitted to the Grants Secretariat at least sixty (60) days before the Project End Date and must set out:

(a) the reasons for the delay, including any circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the Trust;

(b) a revised schedule for completion of the remaining Project activities; and

(c) confirmation that the extension will not result in an increase in the Grant Amount.

The Board shall not be obliged to grant any extension, and the Trust shall continue to comply with all other obligations under this Agreement pending the Board's decision. For the avoidance of doubt, no extension shall operate to extend the period for submission of the Final Report set out in Clause 21.

**20. Variation of Scope**

The Trust shall not make any material change to the scope, objectives, or deliverables of the Project without the prior written consent of the Board. A request for variation shall be submitted in writing, accompanied by a detailed explanation of the proposed change and its impact on the Project timeline, budget, and expected outcomes.

The Board may approve, reject, or approve with conditions any proposed variation. Any approved variation shall be recorded in a written addendum to this Agreement and shall not take effect until such addendum is signed by both parties.

**21. Final Report and Financial Reconciliation**

Within sixty (60) days after the Project End Date, the Trust shall submit to the Grants Secretariat the following:

(a) a final narrative report (the "Final Report") in the format prescribed by the Board, describing the activities undertaken, the outputs delivered, and the outcomes achieved against the objectives set out in the approved Proposal;

(b) a financial report (the "Financial Report") in the format prescribed by the Board, setting out all income and expenditure in respect of the Project, supported by a statement of accounts certified by the Trust's authorised signatory;

(c) a declaration, in the form prescribed by the Board, confirming that the Grant Amount has been applied solely for the purposes of the Project and in accordance with this Agreement; and

(d) copies of all relevant supporting documents, including invoices, receipts, and attendance records, as may be reasonably requested by the Grants Secretariat.

The Financial Report shall reconcile the Grant Amount disbursed to the Trust against verified expenditure. Any unspent portion of the Grant Amount shall be refunded to the Board within thirty (30) days of the Board's acceptance of the Financial Report. The Trust shall not use the Grant Amount to defray any expenditure incurred after the Project End Date unless the Board has given prior written approval.

**22. Final Report Approval and Release of Final Payment**

The final payment under Clause 15 shall be released only after the Board has approved the Final Report and the Financial Report. The Board shall notify the Trust in writing of its decision within sixty (60) days of receipt of the complete reports. If the Board does not approve the reports, it shall provide reasons and afford the Trust a reasonable opportunity to rectify any deficiencies and resubmit.

The Board, through the Grants Secretariat or its authorised representatives, may at any reasonable time, and upon giving the Trust not less than seven (7) days' written notice, inspect the Project premises and the Trust's books, records, and accounts relating to the Project. The Trust shall provide all reasonable assistance and access to such personnel as may be necessary for the conduct of any audit, review, or inspection. Where the Board has reasonable grounds to suspect that the Grant Amount has not been applied in accordance with this Agreement, the Board may undertake an audit or inspection without prior notice.

The Trust shall retain all records, receipts, and supporting documents relating to the Project for a period of not less than five (5) years from the date of the Board's acceptance of the Financial Report. The Trust shall make available, upon request, the original documents and any electronic records for examination and copying.

**24. Intellectual Property**

Where the Project produces any materials, publications, images, or other outputs (collectively, the "Project Outputs"), the Trust shall ensure that the Project Outputs are made available to the public for non-commercial purposes, unless otherwise approved in writing by the Board. The Trust shall acknowledge the support of the Board and the Laksamana Grant Programme in all Project Outputs, in a form approved by the Grants Secretariat. Any copyright or other intellectual property rights in the Project Outputs shall remain with the Trust, subject to a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence in favour of the Board to use the Project Outputs for the purposes of publicity, reporting, and evaluation.

**25. Publicity and Acknowledgement**

The Trust shall not issue any press release, public statement, or promotional material referring to the Grant or the Project without first obtaining the written approval of the Grants Secretariat. The Trust shall ensure that all publicity materials comply with the branding guidelines issued by the Board from time to time. The Trust shall include, in any publication or material produced with the support of the Grant, the statement: "This project is supported by the Laksamana Grant Programme, a Heritage Fund initiative of the Board."

**26. Confidentiality**

The Trust shall keep confidential all information disclosed by the Board in connection with this Agreement and shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Board, except where such disclosure is required by law or by any regulatory authority. This obligation shall survive the termination or expiry of this Agreement.

**27. Data Protection**

The Trust shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (No. 26 of 2012) and any subsidiary legislation in relation to the collection, use, and disclosure of personal data in connection with the Project. The Trust shall put in place appropriate safeguards to protect personal data against unauthorised access, use, or disclosure.

**28. Anti-Bribery and Corruption**

The Trust shall not, and shall ensure that its officers, employees, and agents do not, offer, give, or receive any bribe, kickback, or other improper advantage in connection with the Project or this Agreement. The Trust shall notify the Board immediately if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected breach of this Clause 28.

**29. Conflict of Interest**

The Trust shall declare to the Board, in writing, any actual or potential conflict of interest that arises in connection with the Project, including any interest of the Trust's officers, employees, or board members in any supplier, contractor, or beneficiary of the Project. The Trust shall take all reasonable steps to manage and mitigate any such conflict in accordance with its internal policies and the requirements of the Board.

**30. Termination (continued)**

The Board may terminate this Agreement and suspend the payment of any undisbursed portion of the Grant Amount by giving written notice to the Trust if:

(a) the Trust fails to remedy a material breach of this Agreement within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice of such breach from the Board;

(b) the Trust becomes insolvent, enters into liquidation, or has a receiver or judicial manager appointed over any of its assets;

(c) the Trust ceases to carry on its operations or is unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement;

(d) the Trust provides false or misleading information to the Board in connection with the application for the Grant or the administration of the Grant Amount; or

(e) the Board determines, in its reasonable discretion, that the Project is no longer viable or that the continued disbursement of the Grant Amount would not serve the heritage conservation objectives of the Laksamana Grant Programme.

Upon termination, the Trust shall promptly return to the Board any undisbursed portion of the Grant Amount and shall account for all expenditures incurred up to the date of termination. The Board may require the Trust to repay any portion of the Grant Amount that has been disbursed but not expended in accordance with the Approved Budget and this Agreement.

**31. Force Majeure**

Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement where such failure or delay is caused by an event beyond the reasonable control of that party, including but not limited to fire, flood, storm, epidemic, pandemic, earthquake, civil unrest, war, or any act of government or public authority. The party affected shall notify the other party in writing as soon as practicable and shall take all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact of the event. If the event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either party may terminate this Agreement by giving fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other party.

**32. Notices**

All notices and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered by hand, registered post, or email to the addresses set out in this Agreement. Notices shall be deemed to have been received: if delivered by hand, at the time of delivery; if sent by registered post, on the fifth (5th) business day after posting; and if sent by email, at the time of transmission, provided that no delivery failure notification is received.

**33. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution**

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Singapore. The parties shall use their best efforts to resolve any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement through good-faith negotiations. If the dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of written notice by either party, the dispute shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration in Singapore in accordance with the Arbitration Rules of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ("SIAC") for the time being in force, which rules are deemed to be incorporated by reference into this Clause. The seat of arbitration shall be Singapore. The language of the arbitration shall be English. The Tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator, unless the parties agree otherwise. The decision of the Tribunal shall be final and binding on both parties.

**34. Entire Agreement**

This Agreement, together with the Schedules and any other documents expressly referred to herein, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the Project and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral.

**35. Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
